reviews.classification: standing workflow or mixed-status digest with authority correction
reviews.disposition: AU1–AU15 are standing cost/coverage workflow, not proof of host-enforced quota or measured savings. Preserve one finite shared plan, pilot included, exact unread/truncated spans, fresh short source extractors, cheap supported routing, repair reservations and source/usage/context distinctions. Full-book plan versus exploratory envelope are different scopes. Original cached traffic/account-meter jump and missing launcher are historical audit observations; no new current installation/usage claim or running-worker action follows. Current host restrictions apply to delegation. This reconciliation’s finite document intake does not acquire/read the raw novel corpus or spawn workers; reviewing a source report never upgrades its underlying primary coverage.

reviews.classification: standing workflow or mixed-status digest with authority correction
reviews.disposition: Full digest read separates accepted authority/FLR/process/CX from proposed PRF/FND prompts. FND5’s old sentence, “The content DSL grows only by a second consumer from a second world; otherwise add rows over existing verbs,” conflicted with later accepted AD51 if treated as a prerequisite. Its summary and existing rules-register description now follow AD51: design from known reasonable shared world needs, then validate/revise with a second different world, keeping differences local. FLR route can be a named fixture; human review, installed state, mobile and tracked-dist replacement are not universal technical floor requirements. Content sampling inherits the proven mechanism’s scope, never proof of changed semantics or every scenario.
